correctness.rationale: For n agents with one common strict ranking and uniform bistochastic matrix U=(1/n), Dec-EF of each ordered pair is equivalent to Pr(P(i)>P(j))=1/2. Marginals require at least n supported permutation matchings. If exactly n, all their weights=1/n and odd n cannot make an integral multiple of 1/n equal 1/2. The n+1 impossibility follows because every supported weight<=1/n and for each row exactly one rank is repeated, so exactly two globally sub-1/n weights must correspond to permutations agreeing in every row, contradicting their distinctness. For even n=2m, pair n cyclic shifts of q=(0,...,m-1,2m-1,...,m) through q(k+m)=n-1-q(k) to balance every pair with support n. For odd n>=3, forward cyclic shifts and their distinct rank reversals yield balanced uniform lottery on 2n supports. At n=3, direct six-column marginal equations leave one parameter, and fairness sets it to 1/6 on every permutation, giving unique s(3)=6. Independently recomputed exact 6-variable rational balance system rank 6 and unique uniform weights; boundary n2 and n3 verified. The unknown exact odd n>=5 minimum is explicitly NOT claimed; n+2<=s(n)<=2n only.
